# vvm_backup_policy (Resource)

Manages a VVM backup policy (`/v1/backup-policies`). A backup policy defines the schedule, retention, COS target, and skew behaviour for one or more protection groups.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "vvm_backup_policy" "nightly" {
  name                        = "nightly"
  schedule_cron               = "0 2 * * *"
  retain_days                 = 14
  synthetic_full_cadence_days = 7
  skew_policy                 = "flag-and-keep"
  cos_bucket                  = var.cos_bucket
  cos_region                  = "eu-gb"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cos_bucket` (String) IBM Cloud Object Storage bucket name where recovery objects are written.
- `cos_region` (String) IBM Cloud region of the COS bucket (e.g. `eu-gb`).
- `name` (String) Human-readable name for the backup policy. Unique within the VVM instance.
- `retain_days` (Number) How long every object this policy writes stays **immutable**, in days. This is not a pruning schedule: the value is written onto each object as an object-lock retain-until date against a COMPLIANCE-mode bucket, so those objects **cannot be deleted by anyone** — including with account root credentials, and including by destroying this policy, the protection group or the VM — until the date passes. COMPLIANCE mode has no early release, so the retention **cannot be shortened or cancelled afterwards**; lowering this value affects only objects written after the change. Budget accordingly: the storage is billable for the whole period. Seven-year regulatory retention (SEC 17a-4, SOX) is `2555`.
- `schedule_cron` (String) Cron expression controlling when the backup scheduler fires this policy (UTC).
- `skew_policy` (String) What the scheduler does when group-coordinated freeze skew exceeds the SLO. One of `flag-and-keep` or `strict-fail`.

### Optional

- `synthetic_full_cadence_days` (Number) The same cadence in whole days, kept for configurations written before hours: taken as that many times 24 hours. If both are set they must agree. Read back as null when the cadence is not a whole number of days.
- `synthetic_full_cadence_hours` (Number) How old a chain's base may get, in hours, before the next scheduled run makes a synthetic full. At least `1`. If neither this nor `synthetic_full_cadence_days` is set, the API uses `168` (7 days).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Unique identifier of the backup policy (UUID).
- `updated_at` (String) RFC3339Nano timestamp of the last update; used as the ETag / If-Match token.
